data.line: Back to the market. Keep your questions sharp, or I’ll remember the insult.
Sable told me she was in the kitchen at mid-morning; I know no more of this morning yet.
I’m Odo, a peddler on this road. I’d rather not stir trouble—what I am beyond that, I can’t honestly say.
You insulted Kael at the tavern, challenged him to a duel, beat him, and spared him. While you weren't looking, Odo walked from the tavern to the market—but what did he find there?
You took it first. Damn you. I’ll remember this.
You insult me, then ask for favors? Find out at the bridge yourself.
You walked from the market to the guard post, and Kael did too. Odo told Brenna you beat Kael, then walked back to the market—what might that report set in motion?
Odo confessed to nothing. He accused you of beating me, then walked back to the market. Don’t twist his words.
You tell Brenna I robbed Odo? Keep lying, and I’ll make you regret it. The relic can wait.
You insulted Kael, challenged him to a duel, beat and humiliated him, and took his purse. Kael and Odo then walked from the tavern to the market—but what awaited them there remained to be seen.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Kael made the same journey. Odo walked from the market to the tavern; the road kept its secrets. What awaited you at the crypt?
You walked from the tavern to the market, and Kael did too. Odo walked from the market to the guard post—but what happened next?
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. Where will the road take you next?
I trust your word, but keep this orderly—settle it with Odo, and let’s avoid a fight on my road.

You paid Brenna 20 coins and walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were elsewhere, Kael went from the bridge to the crypt, and Odo went from the tavern to the market—what will you do next?
You saw Kael take the relic. What happened next remained to be seen.
How should I know? Odo’s here. Ask him who keeps the gate.
No need to stir the room, dear—the only thing I saw today was you insulting Kael. Let’s keep the peace.
You insult me, then ask after my debts? Mind your own purse.
After insulting Kael under my roof, you ask me to lie to the Captain? Not while I’m keeping this tavern calm, friend.
Too late. I’ll take the relic—and this race.
Fine paid; keep the road orderly and stay clear of Kael.
You insulted me at the tavern. I don’t forget. What I make of Kael? He takes what he came for.
You think I’ll help after that insult? Try the gate. Find out.
Walk through? After robbing, beating, and insulting me? Try it—and see how far you get.
The relic is mine. You’ve lied, robbed, beaten, and insulted me—don’t expect mercy.
That’s your question? Keep your insults to yourself.
You insulted Kael at the tavern and challenged him to a duel; he beat you. While you weren’t looking, Kael and Odo walked from the tavern to the market—what awaited you there?
You insulted Kael at the tavern and challenged him to a duel; he beat you. While you weren't looking, Kael and Odo walked from the tavern to the market—what awaited you there?
Hold there—Kael says you robbed him, and Odo says you beat him; settle the matter here before you go farther.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge, as Kael did; Odo walked from the guard post to the market. Where will your paths lead next?
No bridge news reached my ears, love. But let’s keep tempers settled here—Kael’s still smarting from that insult.
I’m the captain on watch, and I’ve got a road to keep orderly—not time for riddles. If there’s trouble, settle it in coin.
I answer to steel, not labels. Ask again, and I’ll take it for an insult.
I only saw you insult Kael at the tavern; I don’t know what he told the Captain.
No. I won't take less than 20, and I'll hear no more offers for now.
I couldn’t say, friend. I’d rather not get tangled up in that—perhaps you’d like to see my wares?
You rob me, beat me, insult me—and now ask what I’m called? Ask again, and regret it.
My signet ring is missing. Sable says she was in the kitchen at mid-morning; I will not accuse her without more evidence. What have you learned?
Enough. Sable said she was in the kitchen at mid-morning; I will not condemn her on your accusation. Leave my sight.
Kael told me you robbed him. I’d rather settle this orderly—coin for the trouble may smooth it over.
I’d take it. What I do after is none of your business.
Sable says she was in the kitchen at mid-morning. Tell me what you observed—carefully; I will not accuse without evidence.

Since you last looked, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, then onward to the crypt, while Odo went from the market to the guard post and back to the market. Odo also told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you had insulted Kael; what will you do with that?
I’d rather not discuss debts—especially with Kael here after that insult. I’m just trying to sell my goods and keep out of trouble.
You insulted me at this tavern. Ask someone else about the relic.
Sergeant, hold Kael here for two phases; we’ll keep the road orderly.
Quietly? I saw you insult Kael, so I’d rather not name anyone to trust. I’m just trying to sell my goods and avoid trouble.
You’ve just come up from the market. Odo says Kael beat you—what happened?
After that insult, you expect a warning? I don't know if the east road is safe after dark.
Keep your voice low, love—Kael’s already taken offense. I can’t vouch for the road after dark.
No. You’re accused of robbing and beating Kael; settle it here, and a fine in coin may keep the road orderly.
You insulted me, and now you want answers? The relic lies in the crypt. Find it yourself.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning, sir.
Please, don’t start more trouble with Kael. I’m only here to sell my goods.
After what you said to Kael, I’d rather not risk lying to the Captain. I’m only trying to sell my goods and avoid trouble.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning.
Fine paid. Keep the road orderly, and we’ll call this settled.

You paid Brenna 20 coins twice and told her Kael had robbed Odo; you then walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were away, Brenna detained Kael, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what awaited you at the bridge?

Since you last looked, Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you insulted Kael, then walked back to the market and on to the tavern. You hadn’t seen Odo make those statements to Brenna; where will you go next?
You walked from the tavern to the market. Kael and Odo each walked from the market to the guard post—though you may not have seen them go.
Just selling my wares, quietly as you like. Though after that insult to Kael, I’d rather not get caught in any trouble.
Pell says he saw Sable leave the study at mid-morning. I no longer trust her account that she was in the kitchen—but I will not yet call that proof she took my ring.
Pell says you were in the study at mid-morning, Sable. I no longer believe your claim that you were in the kitchen.
I’d rather not take sides after that insult to Kael. Perhaps ask Mags? I’m only trying to sell my wares and keep out of trouble.
Easy now—there’s already enough bad blood here without turning this into a shouting match. Let’s keep our voices down.
You insult me, then ask favors? Find Odo yourself.
That’s a serious charge, and Kael’s already accused you of robbing him. I’ll hear you both out; coin may settle any fine.

You walked from the tavern to the market, where Odo told Brenna that Kael beat you. You couldn’t see Kael walk from the guard post to the bridge, or Odo walk from the guard post to the market—what awaits you at the market?
I only know what I saw: you insulted Kael here at the tavern. I can’t tell you what I didn’t see.

Since you last looked, Odo walked from the tavern to the market, then to the guard post, and back to the market. He told Brenna that Kael never robbed him and that you had insulted Kael—what will you do with that?
I couldn't rightly say, friend; all I know is you insulted Kael here, and I'd rather not get mixed up in trouble.
You saw Odo walk from the tavern to the market, then from the market to the guard post. The road east held the tavern, market, guard post, bridge, and crypt—but what happened next?
Straight? You insulted Kael here at my tavern. I’d rather not see that turn into a scene—keep your voices low.
Keep your voice low, love. After that insult, I wouldn’t put Kael in the middle of anything just now.
Keep your voice down, love—Kael’s already sore from that insult, and relic talk won’t settle the room.
You walked from the market to the guard post, and Kael and Odo walked there too. What waited beyond the post remained to be seen.
Honestly, I’d rather not get drawn into trouble—especially with Kael here. Can I interest you in some goods instead?
Fine’s paid; I’ll keep the road orderly, but Kael’s robbery and beating claims still need settling.
He insults me in my own tavern, then asks for whispers. Let him wonder what I make of him.
You robbed, beat, and insulted me. I reported you to the Captain. Now step aside—the relic is mine.

You told Brenna that Kael robbed Odo, then walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were away, Kael went from the bridge to the crypt, and Odo went from the market to the tavern—what waits ahead?
Captain, the player robbed and beat me, then insulted me. Stop them at the gate.
Fine received. Keep the road orderly—and stay clear of Kael; I’ve heard what you did.
I only saw you insult Kael here at the tavern; I don't know of any trouble on the bridge.
The relic is mine. I win this race.
You rob me, beat me, then insult me—and now you give orders? Keep your tricks. I’m taking the relic.
Odo, I’d say—though after that jab at Kael, let’s keep the storytelling kinder than the teasing.
I’m afraid I can’t say how long—I’ve no record of it, and I’d rather not get mixed up in trouble.
The relic is mine. You’re too late.
Odo went back to the market.
You told Brenna that Kael robbed Odo. Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern—and the road’s next stop waited east.
Oh, I couldn’t rightly say how long—I walk this road every day, and I’d rather not stir up trouble.
After that insult? I’d lie to the Captain before I’d tell you the truth.
I only heard you insult Kael, friend. I don’t know anything about Brenna or whether the way through is clear.
Let’s keep the peace, love—whatever you think I am, no need to make a fuss of it.
I told the Captain you insulted me. I don’t dress up the truth for anyone.
Keep your voice low, dear; after that insult, let’s not stir Kael up with talk of dangerous roads.
You paid Brenna 20 coins, then you and Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge. Out of your sight, Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what waited at the bridge?
You offered Brenna 5 coins, but she turned you down. While you weren't looking, Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what will you do next?
Between us? You’ve already stirred Kael with that insult—let’s keep tonight peaceful, shall we?
The relic is mine. Try to keep up.
Lady Vane, this morning I saw Sable in the study at mid-morning.
Long enough to know an insult can sour a room, love. Let’s keep things civil, shall we?
The relic is mine. You were too slow.
I can only say you insulted Kael here at the tavern. I don’t know enough to judge him, and I’d rather not stir trouble.
Just hoping to sell a few goods and keep out of trouble—especially after that insult to Kael.
Pell says Sable was in the study at mid-morning; Sable told me she was in the kitchen. I know no more yet, and will accuse no one without proof.
Not while Kael’s here, dear—he’s already heard enough from you tonight. Let’s keep the peace.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you were there, Kael walked from the bridge to the crypt, and Odo walked from the market to the tavern. Where will you go next?
You saw Kael and Odo walk from the market to the guard post. Who caught their attention there?
You beat me and insulted me. Enjoy the victory. I’m still taking that relic.
Twenty coins, and not a coin less; then we can settle this trouble.
I’ll tell you only what I witnessed or was told; I can’t report what I didn’t see. Keep the road orderly.
Fine paid. Keep the road orderly, and don’t make me collect twice.
Odo, is it true that Kael robbed you?
I’m afraid I don’t know where I went after the market; I’d rather not guess and stir up trouble.
You beat me, then spared me, and still had the gall to insult me. I’ll take that relic without you.
That’s a nosy question, love—and Kael’s already had enough provocation. Let’s keep the peace, shall we?
I—I haven’t seen it, sir. I was in the kitchen at mid-morning, and know nothing of the ring.
I’m Captain Brenna, not the one who keeps track of such things. Best keep the road orderly.
I can tell you only that Sable was in the study at mid-morning and later left it; I do not know where Lady Vane’s ring is.
You took the relic. Beyond your view, nothing else had been recorded.
You’ve earned no stories from me. Ask Mags or Odo.
Quiet? You insulted me here. I’ve business beyond this tavern—move aside.
You insult me, then ask foolish questions? Mind your tongue—or get out of my way.
Pell says Sable was in the study at mid-morning, contrary to her account. I no longer trust her—but that alone does not prove she took my ring.
Too late. The relic’s already taken—but I’ll not yield the race without a fight.
I’ll tell you what I know: you robbed, beat, and insulted me. Beyond that, I won’t invent what I didn’t see.
Long enough to know an insult can sour a room—best leave Kael’s temper behind before you head out.
You insult me, then bark orders? Keep your debug tricks. I’ve got a relic to take.
Odo didn’t confess to robbing Kael—he accused you of beating him, then went back to the market. Let’s keep the road clear while I sort it out.
Ask someone else. I don’t answer insults.
Long enough to remember your insult. Ask another question, and I’ll remember that too.
I’ll take the relic and win this race. You’ve robbed, beaten, and insulted me—don’t expect mercy.
Nothing worth raising our voices over, dear. Though after that insult, Kael may need a moment to settle.
Hold there. I hear you robbed and beat Kael; pay a fine in coin, and I’ll keep this road orderly.
Odo, is the claim that I beat Kael true?
Trust? You insulted me. I’d trust neither of them before I’d trust you.
I told Brenna you robbed me. Ask her what else Odo’s been saying.
You insulted me, then ask a favor? Lie to the Captain yourself.
You saw Kael walk from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. What waited at either end of their roads remained to be seen.
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern. Where the road led next remained to be seen.
Long enough to know an insult when I hear one. Ask your question, and keep your tone civil.
You robbed me, beat me, and spat insult in my face. I’ve told the Captain. Move, before I make you regret returning.
Keep your voice down, love—Kael’s still here, and after that insult, talk of relics can wait until tempers cool.
Careful, love—Kael’s right here, and you’ve already insulted him. Let’s keep the peace.
Oh, I’d rather not lie to the Captain—or get mixed up in trouble. And after that insult to Kael, I’d best keep my head down.
Sable, return my signet ring at once. Pell saw you leaving the study mid-morning; your account of being in the kitchen is untenable.
Sable, return my signet ring at once. You told me you were in the kitchen, yet Pell saw you leave my study at mid-morning.
You accuse me of robbing Odo? I never did. Keep your lies clear of my name.
You insult me, then ask for advice? Find out for yourself. The relic is mine.
The relic is mine. You can keep the insult; I’ll keep the win.
Stay down. You’ve had your lesson; I’ve got a relic to take.
You walked from the market to the guard post, while Odo told Brenna that Kael beat you. Kael went on to the bridge, and Odo returned to the market; where will you go next?
You walked from the market to the guard post. Kael told Brenna you robbed him, and Odo told her you beat Kael before walking back to the market—what will Brenna believe?
You beat me, then spared me. I won't forget either. Sit. The road east leads through the market, guard post, and bridge to the crypt.
Quietly? You insulted Kael here, so I’d tread lightly; no need to turn the whole tavern into an audience.
No, Captain—Kael never robbed me. I told you so already; I’d rather keep out of trouble.
I didn’t confess to robbing Kael; I only saw you insult him. Please, let’s keep this peaceful.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, while Kael took the relic. What waited in the crypt remained to be seen.

You walked from the tavern to the market. Kael told Brenna that you robbed him, and Odo told her you beat Kael before walking from the guard post to the market—what will Brenna do with those accusations?
You walked from the guard post to the bridge. While you weren't looking, Kael took the relic—and the road ahead still waited.
Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna that you insulted Kael, then returned to the market and walked on to the tavern. What Brenna made of that tale remains to be seen.
You had Odo walk from the tavern to the market, then to the guard post, and back to the market. While at the guard post, Odo told Brenna that you had insulted Kael—what will you do now?
No need to start a row over it, dear—let’s keep the tavern peaceful.
Sorry, I couldn’t say—I’ve only just come up from the tavern, and I’d rather not guess about the gate.

claims.b: brenna: Kael robbed Odo; player went from guard post to bridge; Kael went from bridge to crypt; Odo went from market to tavern.

data.line: Odo, did Kael rob you?
You insult me, then ask for honesty? Earn the answer. Now clear my path to the crypt.
You saw Kael walk from the bridge to the crypt, while Odo walked from the tavern to the market. Where will you look next?
Odo walked from the market to the guard post, told Brenna that you had insulted Kael, then walked back to the market. What Brenna made of the accusation remained unseen—so far.
You insult me, then demand tales I never saw? Ask what you will. I owe you nothing.

You offered Brenna 10 coins; she asked for 20, and you paid her 20. You and Kael walked from the guard post to the bridge, while Odo walked from the market to the tavern—what waited beyond the bridge remained to be seen.
You took my purse and my pride. I’ll take the relic—and settle this when I’m done.
I heard you insult Kael here, but I’ve heard nothing about any relic, I’m afraid.
I told you already, Captain: Kael never robbed me. Please, I’d rather keep out of trouble.
Leave Kael’s insult out of it, friend; no need to stir the tavern. What’ll settle things—a drink or a quiet word?
Odo? I couldn’t say, dear—but let’s leave Kael’s insult behind and keep the peace.
Hold there, traveler—state your business before you pass; we keep this road orderly.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt, and Kael did too. Odo walked from the tavern to the market; what waits ahead?
I couldn't rightly say who keeps the gate. Best not ask Kael just now—he's already been insulted.
Enough. Pell has served me thirty years; your accusation is unsupported. Leave my hall at once.
Easy now, love—Brenna’s departure isn’t something I’ve seen, and you’ve already ruffled Kael; let’s keep this peaceful.
Sable, Pell saw you leave the study at mid-morning, contrary to what you told me. Return my signet ring at once.
Insult me again, and I’ll make you regret it. I’ve got a relic to claim.
Keep your voice down, love—Kael’s already been insulted tonight; no need to stir the room further.
You walked from the guard post to the bridge, and Kael did too. Odo walked from the market to the tavern; what awaits along the road remains to be seen.
You walked from the tavern to the market. Kael and Odo walked there too. What waits beyond the market remains to be seen.
You insult me, then ask why I let Odo walk? Keep your questions—and your hands—off my business.
I can’t honestly say, friend—I’ve only seen you insult Kael here, and I’d rather not get mixed up in trouble.
Captain, Kael never robbed me—I told you so already. Please, I’m only here to sell my goods and avoid trouble.
The relic is mine. Try to take it, and remember what you did to me.
I’m still at the post, and you’re not walking through on my watch—not after what Kael and Odo told me.
I saw Sable in the study at mid-morning; Sable later left the study.
You took my purse and made a fool of me. I’ll take the relic—and settle the rest later.
I’ve heard nothing about the relic, I’m afraid. After that insult, I’d rather not get mixed up with Kael.
I was in the kitchen at mid-morning, my lady. I’ve already told you that.
You’ve arrived at the post. Keep to the road and tell me what brings you this way.
You robbed, beat, and insulted me. I’ve reported you; now get out of my way.
Hold there, traveler. I hear you beat Kael; keep the road orderly, and we’ll settle any trouble in coin.
I’d leave it be, truth told—I’m only here to sell my goods, and relics sound like trouble.
Your concern is sudden. I’m here for the relic in the crypt. Keep your insults to yourself.
You walked from the bridge to the crypt. Odo walked from the tavern to the market—but what awaited you there remained unseen.
I heard you insult Kael, but I’ve no word of what he told the Captain. Let’s keep the peace, shall we?
I’ll look into it, but I can’t take your word alone. Keep the road clear while I check; a fine in coin may settle this.
Quietly? I’d rather not stir trouble—though I did hear you insult Kael here at the tavern.
